blocks.heading: Coordinating work towards an objective
blocks.text: Effective management means coordinating planning, organising, leading and control so that the business works towards its objectives. An objective supplies the intended result. Planning establishes what needs to happen. Organising allocates the work and resources. Leading helps people carry out the work. Control compares progress with the plan and helps a manager respond to a shortfall. The functions matter because a business normally needs several people and resources to work together. Naming the functions alone leaves out the purpose that makes management effective.

blocks.heading: A workshop with a delivery target
blocks.text: Imagine a small workshop in Namibia that has promised a customer a completed order on Friday. This is an invented teaching situation. Its manager identifies the jobs that must be finished, checks which workers and equipment are available, and allocates the work. Each afternoon the manager compares completed jobs with the schedule. If one stage is late, the manager considers a feasible change to the allocation. The objective is timely completion, rather than merely keeping everyone busy. The example shows the connection between the functions and an intended result. A manager can carry out many activities yet still fail to coordinate them around the objective.

blocks.heading: Connecting the ideas
blocks.text: Organisational structure concerns how responsibilities are arranged. Communication helps people understand a plan. These connections explain why effective management needs more than a job title.
